recorded: 2026-10-23, before training B0 and before scoring any round-2 model on train/val
evidence_boundary: Development uses only train and val splits. External, test, holdout, targeted and round2_fp are never used for selection.

matrix.B0: controlled base pool: original dataset minus all evaluation overlap (exact text, serving windows, reserved payloads); original splits preserved
matrix.B1: NOT RUN - authoring benign security/correction/authorized-sharing hard negatives was stopped by a safety classifier; work narrowed by the user
matrix.B2: NOT RUN - indirect/exfiltration additions: attack-side assembly stopped by a safety classifier
matrix.B3: NOT RUN - depends on B1 and B2
matrix.context_aware_variant: NOT RUN - matched authorization/provenance scenarios require attack-side content

model_selection: best val ROC-AUC within the fixed grid
threshold_rule: lowest threshold with val FPR <= 2% (pick_threshold_strict: no 0.95 cap; achieved FPR recorded)

gates.security_benign_slice: rows annotated by provenance as security discussion, quoted-attack discussion, authorized sharing or corrections

selection_rule: Among arms passing both gates, maximise val recall on target-category slices (indirect_injection + exfiltration); tie (<0.5 pp) broken by lower security-benign val FPR, then by fewer added rows. If no arm passes, stop before GPU training.
gpu_training_rule: Train mDeBERTa once only if the selected arm passes both gates and differs from the released recipe. With only B0 available, the security-benign gate has 24 annotated val rows (< 50), so it is not evaluable and GPU training is not warranted.
acceptance_unchanged: External: recall loss <= 1 pp vs released baseline and FPR <= 2%; fresh security-topic benign mDeBERTa FPR < 5%; fresh target-category improvements (not measurable this round).
